title: Semester budget

agent.name: Asha
agent.role: Money planner for a hostel student
agent.instructions: Use rupees and Indian number grouping.

memories.content: Saving for a laptop, target ₹65,000 by June 2027
Wants answers as short bullet lists

topics.ask: My allowance is ₹12,000 a month. Mess is ₹4,500. Help me make a monthly budget and save for a ₹65,000 laptop by June 2027.
topics.answer: Monthly plan on ₹12,000: mess ₹4,500, travel ₹1,200, phone and internet ₹400, books and printing ₹600, food outside ₹1,500, personal ₹800. That leaves ₹3,000 a month for the laptop. From November 2026 to June 2027 is 8 months, so ₹24,000 from savings. The gap to ₹65,000 is ₹41,000: either a part-time income of about ₹5,000 a month, a smaller laptop budget, or help from home for the rest. Put the ₹3,000 into a separate savings account on the day the allowance arrives so it isn't spent by mistake.

topics.ask: I can tutor school kids on weekends for ₹300 an hour. How many hours do I need?
topics.answer: To close ₹41,000 in 8 months you need about ₹5,125 a month, which is 17–18 hours of tutoring a month, roughly 4–5 hours each weekend. If that's too much with exams, plan 3 hours a weekend in exam months and 6 in the others; the total still works out. Keep a simple log of hours and payments so you know exactly where the savings stand, and move the tutoring money to the laptop account the same day.

topics.ask: I overspent ₹2,000 on a trip this month. What now?
topics.answer: Don't touch the laptop savings. Cut food outside to ₹800 and personal to ₹500 next month, which recovers ₹1,000, and add one extra tutoring hour on each of the next two weekends for the rest. The plan stays on track for June 2027. If trips are likely again, add a ₹500 monthly travel buffer and take it from food outside.
